Key points
• Dietary ﬁber comprises a range of food-borne polysaccharides that share the single physiological property of resistance to
human digestive enzymes.
• These polysaccharides are conﬁned to the intestinal lumen during digestion of food in the upper alimentary tract. Their
presence inﬂuences digestion in ways that depend on their individual physical and chemical properties.
